title: PM/Eng 1:1 prep & follow-ups — API / Console / Dedicated / Private
body:
Purpose: prep for weekly PM↔Eng lead 1:1 — align on risky rollouts, remove blockers, agree owners on experiments across API, Console, Dedicated, Private. Keep it short and actionable.

Meeting length target: 25 minutes.

Agenda (rough timings):
- 0-3m: quick status check + morale (how’s your sprint?)
- 3-8m: production incidents / burn risks (top 2)
- 8-15m: rollout & routing experiment decisions (API + Dedicated)
- 15-20m: Private deployment gating items + Console UX ask
- 20-25m: actions, owners, and calendar items

Current signals and context:
- API: p50 generation latency = 180ms, p95 = 620ms last 24h (region eu-west slightly worse). Token cost/unit trending +7% due to longer average completions on autocomplete prompts.
- Dedicated: 2 customers (ACME & FinScale) trialing reserved pools; ACME reported intermittent tail latency spikes when autoscale triggers (suspect burst serialization).
- Private: Enterprise customer intake (HealthCorp) stalled on network egress policy decision and HSM integration. Security asked for extra audit fields.
- Console: rollout of per-route cost breakdown (beta) picked up confusion: customers expect historical sampling, not point-in-time.

Top items to cover / proposals:
1) Dynamic fallback policy experiment (API):
   - Proposal: route low-SLO requests to cheaper quantized variant when cold-start predicted to exceed 250ms; measure quality delta with A/B on 5% traffic.
   - Data needed: model quality regression threshold (we have eval set but need product signoff); latency prediction accuracy from serving runtime.
   - Decision required: greenlight experiment and assign owner for rollout and rollback hooks.

2) Dedicated autoscale tail spike mitigation:
   - Observed: autoscale times cause queue buildup, then KV cache warm-ups amplify tail latency.
   - Quick fix idea: temporary conservative min-instances + delayed scale-down for first 10m after scale-up.
   - Longer fix: batch/serialize admission window to smooth bursts.
   - Ask to Eng lead: prioritize a 2-day hotfix; who can own and what risk to current deploy cadence?

3) Private deployment gating for HealthCorp:
   - Items blocking: HSM key policy + audit log schema (security wants reqs).
   - Proposed owner split: Security (audit schema) + Platform Eng (HSM connector). Timeline: 3 weeks for HSM connector, 1 week for audit schema.
   - Ask: confirm resource allocation or offer a temporary hosted-proxy alternative (tradeoff: increases compliance review surface).

4) Console UX / Cost breakdown confusion:
   - Short term: add a tooltip and change label to "sampled 24h rolling avg".
   - Longer term: allow calendar-range filters and show sample size.
   - Ask: can Eng ship tooltip + label change in next minor patch (ETA 7 days)?

Open questions I want to surface:
- What’s the confidence interval on the serving runtime’s latency predictor (used for routing decisions)? Is it production-ready for live routing or do we need safety margins?
- For Dedicated autoscale fix: is there a risk of cost blowup if we increase min-instances? If so, what guardrails can we add?
- Private rollout: can we provide HealthCorp with an interim attestation doc while HSM connector is built?

Risks & mitigation notes:
- Risk: fallback to quantized variants reduces output quality for few customer flows (NLG). Mitigation: only enable for short-response prompts and track eval set delta per-customer; immediate rollback if detectable regression.
- Risk: slow autoscale hotfix causes degraded latency for other tenants. Mitigation: release to a canary subset of tenants, monitor p95 and error-rate for 30m.

Decisions I want from eng lead in this 1:1:
- Approve routing-fallback experiment (Y/N); if Y, assign owner and rollout percentage.
- Approve 2-day autoscale hotfix priority and owner.
- Commit to tooltip + label change for Console in next minor.
- Confirm who will be our single point contact for HealthCorp HSM lane.

Action items (pre-meeting prep for me):
- Pull last 7-day latency window split by region and model variant (Asha) — due EOD today.
- Draft experiment README and rollback plan for dynamic fallback (attach to PR) — due tomorrow morning.

Action items to propose during meeting (with tentative owners):
- Kick off routing-fallback experiment: owner = Platform Eng (Mira) — start with 5% traffic; metric checks: p95 latency, eval-quality delta, error-rate. ETA: start next Tue.
- Autoscale hotfix: owner = SRE lead (TBD) — implement conservative min-instances + delayed scale-down. ETA: 48–72 hours after signoff.
- Console tooltip + label: owner = Console FE (Asha) — ship in next minor patch.
- HealthCorp HSM timeline: owner = Platform Eng (Mira) + Security (Samira) — produce HSM plan doc and interim attestation.

Notes to self:
- Be explicit about rollback criteria for the fallback experiment: >2% relative increase in user-reported quality defects on eval set OR p95 increase >10% on production.
- Keep the 1:1 focused — only take decisions we can actually move on this week. If eng lead says no resource, push to a follow-up with prioritization tradeoffs.

Follow-ups (post-meeting):
- Send meeting notes and actions in Slack thread + tag owners.
- Create JIRA tickets with acceptance criteria for the hotfix and routing experiment.
- Block a 30-min review next Thursday to look at first-day experiment telemetry.

Quick data snapshot to reference in meeting:
- API traffic: 1.2M requests/day; avg tokens per request = 72; total token cost/day ~ $1,900 (estimate).
- p50/p95 generation latency (global, last 24h): 180ms / 620ms
- Dedicated pool utilization: ACME 72% sustained, FinScale 55%

Slack snippets to reference:
- "#platform-runtime" thread: summary of p95 spikes (link in linked_artifacts).
- Customer note: HealthCorp compliance ask (internal ticket JIRA-INF-4331).

Bottom line I want from this 1:1: clear greenlights on the experiment + hotfix, owners, and a commitment to a fast follow-up for HealthCorp gating items.

Draft closing line for Slack follow-up after meeting: "Thanks for the time — summary + owners below. I'll create the JIRAs and tag owners; please flag if any ETA is untenable."

-- Noah

Notes to self (private): rough transcript snippets to capture if needed:
- "If Mira can own the fallback, we can ship a small guard-railed experiment within one week."
- "Prefer canary for autoscale fix — we shouldn't touch global config until canary looks good."

End of doc.
